Project context

Object-Oriented Programming · Team of three

  • Java
  • OOP
  • Data structures

Design question

How should a library keep track of who is next when a book or study room is unavailable? We used these everyday requests to explore how different data structures handle ordering and history.

Team contribution

I worked in a three-person team to model users, books, and borrowing records as Java objects. The catalogue starts with 24 books across eight genres. Staff, library members, and guests each have their own menu.

Implementation

Linked lists store the catalogue and borrowing history. A circular queue keeps study room requests in order, and a stack records room usage. Records stay in memory during each session. The submitted source contains a duplicate DoubleNode class declaration that needs to be resolved before the full project compiles.
